projectContext.description: voiceover-matcher-subtitle: AI-powered pipeline for matching voiceover to stock footage

userStories.title: Generate sprint stories for listicle-matching focus area
acceptanceCriteria: Read scripts/ralph/config/ralph-config.json to understand the 'listicle-matching' focus area
Read scripts/ralph/session/prompt.md for project context and architecture notes
Read scripts/ralph/state/queue.json for interview details (story outline, architecture decisions, key files)
Read CLAUDE.md for project conventions and known issues
Analyze the codebase to find 8-12 specific improvements for 'listicle-matching'
Add stories US-71-002 through US-71-012 to scripts/ralph/state/prd.json (MUST use sprint-prefixed IDs)
Each story MUST have 4-6 testable acceptance criteria
Each story MUST have a 'notes' field with: (1) tier classification, (2) exact source file paths, (3) line number ranges if removing/moving code
IMPORTANT: All generated stories MUST have passes set to false - do NOT run tests or evaluate whether they already pass
IMPORTANT: Story IDs MUST follow format US-71-NNN to be unique across sprints
Mark this story (US-71-001) as passes: true when done
userStories.notes: Seed story. Generated 11 stories covering listicle pipeline integration, tag-based scoring, chapter coherence, cross-chapter grouping, listicle-aware scoring, chapter-aware gap analysis, list header count detection, chapter-segment mapping persistence, listicle-to-chapter bridge, chapter-constrained embedding boost, and chapter-type query learning.

userStories.title: Integrate listicle detector into match stage pipeline
acceptanceCriteria: Match stage (src/stages/match.py) calls detect_listicle_structure() on voiceover segments before scoring
Detected ListicleGroup objects are stored on pipeline state (e.g., state.listicle_groups) so downstream stages can access them
When listicle structure is detected, a log message reports the count and labels of detected groups
When no listicle structure is detected, matching proceeds unchanged with no errors
Unit test verifies detect_listicle_structure is called during match stage execution with mock segments
userStories.notes: Tier 1 (Foundation). Wired detect_listicle_groups() into MatchStage.run() via _detect_and_store_listicle_groups() helper. Added listicle_groups field to PipelineState in src/state.py. Logs count and labels when groups detected, gracefully handles errors. 4 unit tests added to tests/test_stage_match.py::TestListicleDetectionIntegration — all pass.

userStories.title: Add tag-based keyword boost to matching scorer
acceptanceCriteria: src/matching/scoring.py has a new apply_tag_keyword_boost() method that compares voiceover segment keywords against video tags
Tag overlap scoring uses graduated boost: 1 tag match -> +0.02, 2 matches -> +0.04, 3+ matches -> +0.06
The adjustment appears in confidence_breakdown as 'tag_keyword_boost' entry
apply_all_adjustments() calls apply_tag_keyword_boost() in the adjustment chain
Unit test verifies graduated boost values for 0, 1, 2, and 3+ tag matches
userStories.notes: Added apply_tag_keyword_boost() with graduated boost (0.02/0.04/0.06). Wired as step 9 in apply_all_adjustments. 10 tests pass.

userStories.title: Add chapter coherence penalty for scattered source usage
acceptanceCriteria: src/matching/scoring.py has a new apply_chapter_coherence_penalty() method
When a voiceover chapter uses segments from >5 different video sources, a penalty of -0.03 is applied per excess source
The penalty is capped at -0.10 to avoid over-penalizing
The adjustment appears in confidence_breakdown as 'chapter_coherence' entry
Config option matching.chapter_grouping.coherence_penalty_threshold (default 5) controls the threshold
Unit test verifies penalty triggers at threshold and caps correctly
userStories.notes: All 6 criteria met. Implementation + 11 unit tests pass (threshold trigger, cap at -0.10, config option, breakdown entry, disabled check).

userStories.title: Build cross-chapter relevance matrix for candidate boosting
acceptanceCriteria: New function compute_relevance_matrix() in src/matching/scoring.py or src/chapter_detection/ computes voiceover_chapter x video_chapter topic overlap scores
Relevance scores are normalized to 0-1 range based on keyword intersection over union
Config option matching.chapter_grouping.relevance_boost_weight (default 0.1) controls the boost magnitude
Candidates from high-relevance video chapters get a soft boost proportional to relevance score * weight
Unit test verifies matrix computation with known keyword sets produces expected overlap scores
userStories.notes: HARD STORY: Skipped after 3_failures - pending decomposition

userStories.title: Add listicle-aware scoring adjustment for within-group consistency
acceptanceCriteria: src/matching/scoring.py has a new apply_listicle_consistency_boost() method
Segments within the same ListicleGroup that match from the same video source get a +0.04 boost
Segments at listicle group boundaries (first segment of a new group) get no boost or penalty
The adjustment appears in confidence_breakdown as 'listicle_consistency' entry
apply_all_adjustments() calls apply_listicle_consistency_boost() when listicle_groups are available
Unit test verifies boost applied within groups and not across group boundaries
userStories.notes: All 6/6 criteria verified. 8 tests pass. Implementation + tests complete.

userStories.title: Add chapter-aware gap prioritization to iterative match
acceptanceCriteria: src/iterative_match/gap_analyzer.py analyze_gaps() annotates each gap with its containing voiceover chapter/listicle group
Gaps in introduction chapters (first 10% of segments) get priority_boost of +0.2
Gaps in conclusion chapters (last 10% of segments) get priority_boost of +0.15
Gap priority is used to sort gap-filling order so high-importance chapters are filled first
Unit test verifies gaps in intro/conclusion get higher priority than gaps in middle sections
userStories.notes: All 5/5 criteria verified: (1) chapter annotation in analyze_gaps, (2) intro +0.2 boost, (3) conclusion +0.15 boost, (4) priority sorting for gap-filling order, (5) 9 unit tests passing.

userStories.title: Add list header count detection to listicle detector
acceptanceCriteria: src/chapter_detection/listicle_detector.py detects list header patterns like 'top 10', '5 reasons', '3 ways', 'seven tips'
When a list header is detected, the expected_count is stored on the detection result
The detector logs a warning when detected item count differs from expected_count by more than 1
Both numeric ('5 reasons') and word-form ('five reasons') counts are recognized
Unit test verifies detection of at least 4 different header patterns with correct expected_count extraction
userStories.notes: HARD STORY: Skipped after 3_failures - pending decomposition

userStories.title: Persist chapter-segment mapping in checkpoint for output stage
acceptanceCriteria: Chapter detection results (VideoChapter list and ListicleGroup list) are serialized to checkpoint.json after match stage
Chapter data survives pipeline resume -- loading checkpoint restores chapter/listicle structures
Output stage can read chapter/listicle data from checkpoint to annotate timeline markers
Backward compatibility: loading a checkpoint without chapter data produces empty lists, not errors
Unit test verifies round-trip serialization of VideoChapter and ListicleGroup through checkpoint
userStories.notes: Added chapter_data field to CheckpointData, serialize chapters/listicle groups in match stage save, restore on resume, backward compat with empty dict, 8 unit tests pass.

userStories.title: Bridge listicle groups to voiceover chapter structure for unified handling
acceptanceCriteria: New function in src/chapter_detection/ converts ListicleGroup objects into VoiceoverChapter objects for unified downstream handling
Converted chapters have topic_keywords populated from the ListicleGroup topic_keywords field
When both YouTube chapters and listicle groups are detected, they are merged with YouTube chapters taking precedence for overlapping ranges
The unified chapter list is available to scoring adjustments via the same interface as regular chapters
Unit test verifies conversion from listicle groups to chapters and merge behavior with overlapping ranges
userStories.notes: Tier 2 (Integration). Currently, listicle detection (src/chapter_detection/listicle_detector.py) and chapter detection (src/chapter_detection/detector.py) produce separate data structures. The design doc Area 3+4 says 'Both can coexist (voiceover structure + video chapter structure)'. This story creates the bridge so scoring adjustments (chapter_topic_match, chapter_source_consistency) work uniformly regardless of whether structure came from YouTube chapters or listicle detection. VoiceoverChapter model is in src/chapter_detection/models.py.

userStories.title: Add chapter-constrained candidate boost to embedding search
acceptanceCriteria: src/matching/embedding_search.py applies a soft boost to candidates whose video chapter has high relevance to the current voiceover chapter
The boost is proportional to relevance_score * relevance_boost_weight (default 0.1)
Candidates without chapter information receive no boost or penalty (neutral treatment)
The boost is applied as a score adjustment after FAISS similarity retrieval, not as a filter
Unit test verifies candidates from relevant video chapters rank higher than equal-similarity candidates from irrelevant chapters
userStories.notes: Tier 3 (Matching Enhancement). Depends on US-71-005 (relevance matrix). From Area 5 of the design doc: 'When voiceover has chapter structure, boost candidates from video chapters with high relevance score. Not a hard filter, but a soft boost.' The embedding_search.py currently does basic FAISS similarity search and returns (segment, score) tuples. This adds a post-retrieval re-scoring step using the relevance matrix. Config via matching.chapter_grouping.relevance_boost_weight.

userStories.title: Add chapter-type-aware query learning to iterative match
acceptanceCriteria: src/iterative_match/query_learning.py tracks query success rates bucketed by chapter type (intro, body, conclusion, listicle_item)
When generating new queries for a gap, the chapter type of the gap is used to prefer historically successful query patterns for that type
Chapter type classification uses simple position-based heuristics: first 10% = intro, last 10% = conclusion, listicle items from detector, remainder = body
Query learning data persists across iterative match rounds within the same pipeline run
Unit test verifies that query patterns successful for 'intro' chapters are preferred when filling intro gaps
userStories.notes: Tier 3 (Iterative Match Enhancement). From Area 6 of the design doc. The query_learning.py at src/iterative_match/query_learning.py already tracks query success/failure but does not differentiate by chapter type. This adds a chapter_type dimension to the learning storage. The chapter type comes from the voiceover chapter structure detected in the match stage (US-71-002/US-71-010). Simple position heuristics avoid dependency on chapter detection for basic classification.
